title: snapshot_structured's 'never raises' contract is held by seven other modules, not by its own gather
repro: design - add an eighth disclosure-only cross-check to the fan-out without its own try/except and every research path (FAST bundle, DEEP, ULTRA, tier-B) raises out of snapshot_structured; only DEEP has a caller-side except.
notes: Pull complexity downward: the docstring promises 'this never raises' and the obligation is pushed outward to every current and future cross-check author. The gather that owns the promise is the one place that can hold it. Smallest fix: `results = await asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True)` plus a coercion of any BaseException to None before the `if x is not None` folds below.

title: run_deep_brief documents stale wall defaults and its clamp cannot express ULTRA's own default
repro: run_deep_brief(q, depth='ultra', wall_seconds=360) -> _clamp(360, 30, 300, 360) returns 300, silently cutting the profile's own default; run_deep_brief(q, depth='ultra') -> _clamp(None, ...) hits the TypeError branch and returns 360 unclamped. Two callers asking for the same thing get different budgets. The docstring says deep 120 / ultra 240; depth.py says 180 / 360.
notes: Comment duplicating a value that has since moved, plus a validation ceiling that predates the R13/R9 bumps it now silently contradicts. Consequence: an explicit wall_seconds equal to the documented default is silently reduced by 60s on ULTRA. Smallest fix: clamp against max(300, profile.wall_seconds) (or the profile's own ceiling) and delete the numbers from the docstring in favour of naming depth.PROFILES.

refuter.reason: Confirmed: _clamp(360, 30, 300, 360) returns 300 while _clamp(None, ...) hits the TypeError path and returns the profile's 360 unclamped; the docstrings at deep_research.py:404-405 and research.py:195-196 still say deep 120 / ultra 240 vs depth.py's 180/360. Scope correction: the defect is wider than stated - the model-facing tool schema (catalog.py:369-372) advertises wall_seconds default 120, range 30-300, so any model-supplied value (the handler forwards args.get('wall_seconds') at research.py:198) caps ULTRA at 300 and a schema-default 120 leaves the heavy panel max(60, 120-90)=60s. Severity kept medium because how often models send the arg is unmeasured.

title: DuckDuckGo is paced twice by two independently-tuned throttles in two files
repro: design (code read): on the keyless path every DDG hit passes through get_queue().acquire('ddg') at keyless.py:220 (ENGINE_MIN_INTERVALS['ddg'] = 3.0, pacing.py:33) AND _get_bucket().acquire() at ddg.py:384 (_RATE_PER_MIN = 20, i.e. one per 3.0s, ddg.py:69). The Lite fallback takes a second bucket token at ddg.py:391, so one DDG search consumes two of the ~20/min budget.
notes: Information leakage: 'how fast may we hit DuckDuckGo' is one design decision expressed as two numbers in two modules that happen to agree today (3.0s vs 60/20 = 3.0s). Nothing links them, so the next tuning pass changes one and the effective rate silently becomes the min of two disagreeing policies. Concrete consequence on top of the drift risk: the duplication is pure added latency on the primary engine, and it compounds finding 6. Smallest fix: delete ddg.py's _TokenBucket/_get_bucket and its two acquire calls -- pacing.RequestQueue already covers every engine including the bare-ddg fallback lane once registry._build_ddg routes through it.

refuter.reason: Real and self-admitted: pacing.py:31-32 says 'DDG ~3s mirrors the existing ~20/min token bucket in ddg.py', and both throttles run (keyless.py:220, ddg.py:384/391). Severity lowered: the bucket starts full with capacity 20 (ddg.py:74, _TokenBucket init) and RequestQueue already spaces DDG at 3s, so the bucket only adds latency after sustained Lite-fallback double-spends. This is a drift and maintenance risk, not a normal-use defect.
